# Intraday realized skew - report

**Slug:** `family-realized-skew`
**Window:** 2016-01-04 -> 2023-12-29, development only. The 2024-2026
holdout was never loaded. A separate process deposited `holdout.json` / `holdout_run.log` in this folder after the development run; this agent did not read or use them.
**Execution:** `research/bt.py`, 1-minute marks, next-open fills, 2% band,
long-only, weights >= 0, sum <= 1. Headline 1 bp; 5 bp and 10 bp also reported.
**Primary:** QQQ 5-minute realized skew, trailing 10-session mean. If
S10 < -0.10, hold TQQQ for 3 sessions; otherwise BIL. A new signal rolls the
exit forward.

---

## 1. Headline

| cost | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | Sortino | vol | TQQQ exposure | fills | turnover |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **1 bp** | **40.66%** | **54.71%** | **0.99** | 1.42 | 44.7% | **54.4%** | 331 | 2,515x |
| 5 bp | 38.35% | 56.13% | 0.95 | 1.36 | 44.7% | 54.4% | 331 | 2,298x |
| 10 bp | **35.51%** | 57.85% | 0.91 | 1.30 | 44.7% | 54.4% | 331 | 2,056x |

The stated bar is TQQQ **36.72% CAGR / 82.29% max DD / 0.82 Sharpe**. The
local 1-minute benchmark is 36.15% / 82.29% / 0.80.

**The primary clears 1 bp and 5 bp but fails 10 bp (35.51% vs 36.72%).** That
is kill criterion #3, and it is a real fail, not a rounding issue. The
headline is a marginal pass, not a robust one.

Ending equity at 1 bp is **$1,524,613** from $100,000. The sleeve is in TQQQ
54.4% of bars and BIL 45.6%.

Daily-return correlation to TQQQ is **0.668**; correlation to the nine current
winners ranges from **0.451 to 0.730**.

## 2. Benchmarks

| | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | Calmar | TQQQ exposure |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| primary 1 bp | 40.66% | 54.71% | 0.99 | 0.74 | 54.4% |
| TQQQ | 36.15% | 82.29% | 0.80 | 0.44 | 100% |
| QQQ | 18.91% | 37.30% | 0.90 | 0.51 | - |

## 3. Yearly returns and exposure

| year | strategy | TQQQ | TQQQ exposure | note |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 2016 | +34.5% | +19.9% | 38.5% | early skew events |
| 2017 | +95.1% | +114.5% | 72.9% | close to TQQQ |
| 2018 | **+40.5%** | -20.8% | 40.2% | defensive |
| 2019 | +52.5% | +148.2% | 55.6% | badly lags |
| 2020 | +183.2% | +104.1% | 63.6% | crash-recovery |
| 2021 | **-6.0%** | +81.1% | 52.0% | loses money in a bull year |
| 2022 | **-36.9%** | -79.4% | 37.5% | loses less than TQQQ |
| 2023 | +57.1% | +192.0% | 74.8% | badly lags |

The profile is uneven. It is defensive in 2018 and 2022, but it actually loses
money in 2021 (-6.0%) and lags badly in 2019, 2021 and 2023. The strategy is
not a consistent TQQQ-beater; it is a negative-skew sleeve with a few very
good crash-recovery years.

## 4. What the signal actually trades

849 event days, 83 closed episodes. The event-forward return is the TQQQ
open-to-open return over the 3 sessions after the signal.

| statistic | event-forward (3 sessions) | closed episodes |
|---|---:|---:|
| n | 848 | 83 |
| mean | **+0.84%** | +4.19% |
| median | +1.08% | +4.21% |
| win rate | 58.8% | 66.3% |
| t-stat | **3.82** | 2.85 |
| bootstrap p(mean <= 0) | - | 0.0017 |
| 95% CI | - | +1.33% .. +7.08% |
| worst / best | -30.1% / +27.4% | -27.7% / +44.7% |

The event-level edge is positive and statistically strong (t = 3.82), but the
events are **highly overlapping**: 849 event days cluster into 83 episodes
because a negative-skew regime persists for days. The independent evidence is
closer to 83 episodes than 849 events. The episode-level t is 2.85, still
positive but less impressive.

The distribution of S10 is centred at **-0.043** (min -0.888, max +0.734), so
the -0.10 threshold selects roughly the lower half of the distribution, not a
rare tail. This is a regime sleeve, not a rare-event strategy.

## 5. Pre-registered 8-cell grid

All at 1 bp, 1-minute marks. The primary is cell 1.

| # | S10 threshold | hold | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | TQQQ exp | fills |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | **-0.10** | **3** | **40.66%** | **54.71%** | **0.99** | **54.4%** | 331 |
| 2 | -0.05 | 3 | 38.33% | 69.1% | 0.92 | 62.4% | 323 |
| 3 | -0.15 | 3 | **21.08%** | 62.2% | 0.67 | 46.4% | 347 |
| 4 | -0.20 | 3 | **16.77%** | 52.9% | 0.61 | 36.8% | 315 |
| 5 | -0.10 | 2 | 34.01% | 61.0% | 0.90 | 49.4% | 403 |
| 6 | -0.10 | 4 | 43.50% | 61.7% | 1.02 | 58.4% | 283 |
| 7 | -0.10 | 5 | 42.13% | 59.5% | 0.98 | 61.9% | 255 |
| 8 | -0.10 | 6 | 44.65% | 62.2% | 1.00 | 65.1% | 231 |

**5 of 8 cells clear the bar** - exactly the minimum for the plateau test.
The failures are informative:

- The **extreme negative tail fails badly**: -0.15 -> 21.08%, -0.20 -> 16.77%.
  A crash-skew session is not a buy signal. This is the opposite of the naive
  "more negative skew -> bigger bounce" reading, and it is the most important
  finding in this family.
- The short hold (h2) fails at 34.01%; h4/h5/h6 all pass at 42-45%. The
  effect needs 4-6 sessions, not 2.
- The mild threshold (-0.05) passes at 38.33% but with a 69.1% drawdown.

The primary is not a single-cell spike, but the threshold dimension is a
one-sided ridge: only the mild-negative region works.

## 6. Subperiods and drawdown anatomy

| period | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | TQQQ exp |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016-2019 | 51.82% | 29.6% | 1.42 | 51.7% |
| 2020-2021 | 65.90% | 39.6% | 1.21 | 57.7% |
| 2022-2023 | **1.34%** | 44.7% | 0.29 | 56.0% |
| ex-2020 | **24.04%** | 54.7% | 0.75 | 46.4% |
| ex-2022 | 49.58% | 39.6% | 1.23 | 49.7% |

**Ex-2020 CAGR is 24.04%, which triggers kill criterion #6 (<= 25%).** The
strategy is a 2020-dependent sleeve: 2020 alone returns +183.2%, and without
it the CAGR is below TQQQ and below the 25% floor. The 2022-2023 cut is
+1.34%, essentially flat over two years.

**Worst drawdowns:**

| peak -> trough | depth | context |
|---|---:|---|
| 2021-02-17 -> 2022-11-09 | **-54.7%** | long through the 2021-2022 bear; the negative-skew regime stays on |
| 2020-09-03 -> 2020-09-21 | -38.3% | September 2020 growth sell-off |
| 2020-02-25 -> 2020-02-28 | -31.9% | the first COVID crash week |

The maximum drawdown is a 21-month bear-market grind, not a single crash.
Negative skew persists through a bear market, so the sleeve stays long and
compounds down. That is the family's structural weakness.

## 7. Placebo

Two placebos, each 100 full 1-minute backtests:

| | mean CAGR | sd | p95 | max | p(real >= placebo) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| circular shift of the target | 21.6% | 14.7% | 45.2% | 61.6% | **0.08** |
| random event days | 30.5% | 11.1% | 49.5% | 56.1% | **0.17** |

Neither placebo rejects at 5%. The shift placebo is closer (p = 0.08), but its
p95 is 45.2%, *above* the real 40.66%. The random-entry placebo runs at 80.3%
average exposure (vs 54.4% real), so it has more beta and is not
exposure-matched; it still beats the real strategy 17% of the time.

The honest conclusion: the event-level skew edge is real (t = 3.82), but the
portfolio timing is **not statistically distinguishable from a random
long-biased sleeve** at conventional thresholds.

## 8. Correlation to the nine current winners

| winner | correlation |
|---|---:|
| relative-value-tqqq | 0.730 |
| family-rebalance-flow | 0.694 |
| family-ml-microstructure | 0.648 |
| vol-scaled-crash-stop | 0.608 |
| family-short-reversal | 0.605 |
| ratio-froth | 0.570 |
| family-session-timing | 0.552 |
| fomc-opex-window | 0.521 |
| family-intraday-microstructure-day | 0.451 |
| TQQQ | 0.668 |

All nine correlations are below 0.85; the maximum is 0.73. The skew sleeve is
moderately correlated with relative-value and rebalance-flow, but not a
duplicate. The stored winner curves were truncated at 2023-12-29 before any return was computed; no 2024-2026 value was inspected.

## 9. Causality and implementation

- Each session's realized skew uses 5-minute closes from 09:34 to 15:59 ET.
  The 10-day mean ends at the 15:59 close of day d; the target fills at the
  next 09:30 open. No 16:00 print is used.
- The overnight gap is excluded by construction.
- Truncating the panel at the **2020-03-12 11:07** cut leaves **409,376**
  prior weights identical: `max_abs_weight_diff = 0.0`.
- No full-sample normalisation, no volatility scaling, no moving average, no
  drawdown/capitulation event, no calendar clock, no opening-range/VWAP, no
  relative strength, no ML.
- Long-only, weights are 0 or 1, sum <= 1, BIL is the flat asset. 2% band;
  331 fills; 1 bp headline plus 5/10 bp.
- The result is deterministic; the only randomness is the placebo, seeded at
  11.

## 10. Kill criteria - verdict

| # | criterion | value | triggered? |
|---:|---|---:|---|
| 1 | 1 bp CAGR <= 36.72% or DD >= 82.29% | 40.66% / 54.71% | no |
| 2 | fewer than 5/8 grid cells pass | 5/8 | no |
| 3 | 10 bp CAGR <= 36.72% | **35.51%** | **yes** |
| 4 | shift-placebo p > 0.05 | **0.08** | **yes** |
| 5 | random-entry placebo p > 0.05 | **0.17** | **yes** |
| 6 | ex-2020 CAGR <= 25% | **24.04%** | **yes** |
| 7 | correlation to a winner > 0.85 | 0.730 max | no |
| 8 | < 100 fills or < 30 events | 331 / 849 | no |
| 9 | pre-cut max weight diff > 1e-12 | 0.0 | no |
| 10 | event-forward t <= 1.5 | 3.82 | no |

**Verdict: marginal / not validated.** Four of the ten kill criteria are
triggered: 10 bp cost, both placebos, and the ex-2020 floor. The event-level
skew premium is real and statistically strong, but the portfolio expression is
too close to a long-biased random sleeve, too dependent on 2020, and too
expensive at 10 bp. The family is an honest negative-to-marginal result: the
statistical object is interesting, the tradable edge is not robust.
hypothesis_md:
# Intraday realized skew - `family-realized-skew`

**Window:** 2016-01-04 -> 2023-12-29, development only. The 2024-2026
holdout is never loaded.

**Family:** realized skewness / semivariance asymmetry of intraday returns.
The primary object is the skew, not the volatility level.

---

## 1. Mechanism

Realized skew measures the asymmetry of the intraday return distribution. A
negative-skew session has many small up moves and a few large down moves; a
positive-skew session has the opposite. The skewness premium says assets with
negative skew must offer higher expected returns, and the lottery literature
says positive-skew assets are overpriced. The family hypothesis is therefore:

- negative realized skew -> a bounce / higher forward return;
- positive realized skew -> continuation or fragility (lower forward return).

The signal is deliberately built from **5-minute intraday returns**, so the
overnight gap does not enter the skew. The overnight gap is a separate object
(and is already used by the gap families).

The development scan found that the negative-skew bounce is real at the event
level but only in the **mild** negative range. Extreme negative skew (the
crash tail, S10 < -0.15 or -0.20) is followed by *worse* returns, not better
ones: a crash-skew session is a warning, not a buy signal. The primary
threshold is therefore -0.10, the mild-negative region, and the report states
that the extreme-tail version fails.

## 2. Exact rules

### Estimation window and decision clock

```
5-minute closes: 09:34, 09:39, ..., 15:59 ET
r5[j]  = log(close5[j] / close5[j-1])            (77 returns per full session)
RS[d]  = mean(r5^3) / mean(r5^2)^1.5             (per-session realized skew)
S10[d] = mean(RS[d-9..d])                        (trailing 10 sessions)
```

`S10[d]` uses only sessions through the 15:59 close of day d. The overnight
gap is excluded. Sessions with fewer than 10 five-minute returns (half-days,
data holes) are skipped; the 10-day mean uses the available sessions.

### Position rule (known at 15:59 of d; fill at the next 09:30 open)

```
if S10[d] < -0.10:
    TQQQ 1.0 for the next 3 sessions
else:
    BIL 1.0
```

A new signal while holding rolls the 3-session exit forward. The position is
0 or 1; there is no volatility scaling and no volatility filter.

### Execution

`research/bt.py`, 1-minute marks, next-open fills, 2% band, long-only,
weights >= 0, sum <= 1. Headline cost 1 bp; 5 bp and 10 bp also reported. BIL is
the flat asset.

## 3. Pre-registered 8-cell grid

The grid was fixed before the final run. It varies the skew threshold at the
primary 3-session hold, and the hold at the primary threshold.

| # | S10 threshold | hold | role |
|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | **-0.10** | **3** | **primary** |
| 2 | -0.05 | 3 | shallower |
| 3 | -0.15 | 3 | deeper |
| 4 | -0.20 | 3 | extreme tail |
| 5 | -0.10 | 2 | short hold |
| 6 | -0.10 | 4 | longer hold |
| 7 | -0.10 | 5 | longer hold |
| 8 | -0.10 | 6 | longer hold |

## 4. Falsifiers

The family is rejected, or downgraded to marginal, if any of these hold on
dev:

1. Primary 1 bp CAGR <= 36.72% or max drawdown >= 82.29%.
2. Fewer than 5 of the 8 grid cells clear the same bar.
3. 10 bp CAGR <= 36.72%.
4. Shift-placebo p > 0.05.
5. Random-entry placebo p > 0.05.
6. Ex-2020 CAGR <= 25%.
7. Daily-return correlation to any of the nine current winners > 0.85.
8. Fewer than 100 fills or fewer than 30 independent events.
9. Pre-cut max weight difference > 1e-12.
10. The event-forward 3-session return is not significantly positive
    (t <= 1.5), which would mean the skew premium is not present at the event
    level.

## 5. Expected failure modes

- **Extreme-tail failure:** the deepest negative-skew sessions are crash
  sessions; buying them should be worse, not better. The -0.15 and -0.20 grid
  cells are the test.
- **Ex-2020 dependence:** the 2020 crash-recovery should carry a large share
  of the return; ex-2020 is reported.
- **Overlap with short reversal:** negative skew is correlated with down
  days, so the daily correlation to `family-short-reversal` should be
  moderately high (0.5-0.7).
- **Weak placebo:** the event count is large (849) but highly overlapping, so
  the event t-stat overstates the independent evidence. The portfolio placebo
  is the honest test.
- **Cost sensitivity:** 2,500x turnover at 1 bp; the 10 bp case is the stress.

## 6. What this is not

- Not volatility targeting: the position is 0 or 1; the signal is the third
  moment, not the second.
- Not a volatility filter: no VIX, no realized-vol level and no vol regime.
- Not a 20/50/100/150/165/200-day moving-average trend gate.
- Not a drawdown / capitulation event: no peak-to-trough state machine.
- Not a calendar clock, opening-range, VWAP or relative-strength rule.
- Not ML.

## 7. Design provenance

The daily realized skew and the 10-day mean were computed on the development
window only. A coarse scan tested the daily skew, the 5-day mean and the
10-day mean at thresholds from -2.0 to 0.0. The extreme negative thresholds
produced few events and negative forward returns; the mild negative threshold
(-0.10 on the 10-day mean) produced the stable positive event edge. The
threshold/hold grid above was then frozen, and the final run was made once. No
2024-2026 data was loaded at any point. The failure of the extreme tail is
reported as a finding, not hidden.

"""Intraday realized skew - `family-realized-skew`.

DEVELOPMENT WINDOW ONLY (2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29).  The 2024-2026 holdout is
never loaded.

Primary object
--------------
Realized skewness of QQQ 5-minute intraday log returns, pooled over the
trailing 10 sessions:

    r5[j]   = log(close5[j] / close5[j-1])       (5-minute closes, 09:34-15:59)
    RS[d]   = mean(r5^3) / mean(r5^2)^1.5        (per session)
    S10[d]  = mean(RS[d-9..d])

The overnight gap is excluded.  Negative realized skew means the session's
downside tail dominates (many small up moves, a few large down moves).

Rule (known at the 15:59 close of d; fills at the next 09:30 open):
    S10[d] < -0.10 -> TQQQ 1.0 for the next 3 sessions
    otherwise      -> BIL 1.0
A new signal while holding rolls the 3-session exit forward.

The primary object is the skew, not the volatility level.  There is no
volatility targeting and no volatility filter.

Run:
    $env:PYTHONPATH = "C:\\Users\\27175\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\opencode\\pylibs"
    $env:BT_THREADS = "1"
    python research/new/family-realized-skew/strategy.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "research"))
import bt  # noqa: E402

DEV_START, DEV_END = "2016-01-04", "2023-12-29"
BARS_PER_YEAR = 252 * 390
WARM = 20
OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SLUG = "family-realized-skew"

PARAMS = dict(skew_thr=-0.10, hold=3, look=10, min_daily_returns=20)

WINNERS = [
    "ratio-froth", "vol-scaled-crash-stop", "relative-value-tqqq",
    "fomc-opex-window", "family-session-timing", "family-short-reversal",
    "family-rebalance-flow", "family-intraday-microstructure-day",
    "family-ml-microstructure",
]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# daily features
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def daily_features(ts, o, c):
    dates, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    nd = len(first)
    qc = c[last, 0]
    r1 = np.r_[np.nan, qc[1:] / qc[:-1] - 1.0]
    rsk = np.full(nd, np.nan)
    rv = np.full(nd, np.nan)
    for i in range(nd):
        s = c[first[i]:last[i] + 1, 0]
        if len(s) < 20:
            continue
        c5 = s[4::5]
        r5 = np.diff(np.log(c5))
        if len(r5) < 10:
            continue
        m2 = float(np.mean(r5 ** 2))
        m3 = float(np.mean(r5 ** 3))
        if m2 <= 0:
            continue
        rsk[i] = m3 / m2 ** 1.5
        rv[i] = m2
    return dict(dates=dates, sess_dates=dates[first], first=first, last=last,
                nd=nd, qc=qc, r1=r1, rsk=rsk, rv=rv,
                tq=c[last, 1], tqo=o[first, 1], bil=c[last, 2])


def skew_state(f, params):
    p = dict(PARAMS)
    if params:
        p.update(params)
    look = int(p["look"])
    s = pd.Series(f["rsk"]).rolling(look, min_periods=look).mean().to_numpy()
    mask = s < float(p["skew_thr"])
    mask[:WARM] = False
    mask[~np.isfinite(s)] = False
    pos = np.zeros(f["nd"])
    until = -1
    event_days = []
    for d in range(f["nd"]):
        if mask[d]:
            event_days.append(d)
            until = max(until, d + int(p["hold"]))
        if d < until:
            pos[d] = 1.0
    return pos, event_days, s


def weights_from_pos(ts, f, pos):
    n = len(ts)
    w = np.zeros((n, 3))
    w[:, 2] = 1.0
    prev = 0.0
    for d in range(f["nd"]):
        target = float(pos[d])
        a, b = int(f["first"][d]), int(f["last"][d])
        w[a:b + 1, 1] = prev
        w[a:b + 1, 2] = 1.0 - prev
        w[b, 1] = target
        w[b, 2] = 1.0 - target
        prev = target
    return w


def episodes(f, pos):
    runs = []
    d = 0
    nd = f["nd"]
    while d < nd:
        if pos[d] <= 0:
            d += 1
            continue
        s = d
        while d < nd and pos[d] > 0:
            d += 1
        e = d - 1
        en = s + 1
        ex = min(e + 2, nd - 1)
        if en >= nd:
            continue
        runs.append((s, e, float(f["tqo"][en]), float(f["tqo"][ex])))
    return runs


def episode_stats(runs):
    rs = np.array([b / a - 1.0 for _, _, a, b in runs if a > 0 and b > 0])
    if len(rs) < 3:
        return {"n": int(len(rs))}
    t = float(rs.mean() / rs.std(ddof=1) * np.sqrt(len(rs))) if rs.std(ddof=1) > 0 else None
    rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
    boot = rng.choice(rs, (10000, len(rs)), replace=True).mean(axis=1)
    return {"n": int(len(rs)), "mean": float(rs.mean()),
            "median": float(np.median(rs)), "win": float((rs > 0).mean()),
            "t": t, "bootstrap_p": float((boot <= 0).mean()),
            "ci95_low": float(np.quantile(boot, 0.025)),
            "ci95_high": float(np.quantile(boot, 0.975)),
            "worst": float(rs.min()), "best": float(rs.max())}


def forward_event_stats(f, days, hold):
    rs = []
    nd = f["nd"]
    for d in days:
        en = d + 1
        ex = min(d + 1 + int(hold), nd - 1)
        if en >= nd:
            continue
        rs.append(float(f["tqo"][ex] / f["tqo"][en] - 1.0))
    rs = np.asarray(rs, dtype=float)
    if len(rs) < 3:
        return {"n": int(len(rs))}
    t = float(rs.mean() / rs.std(ddof=1) * np.sqrt(len(rs))) if rs.std(ddof=1) > 0 else None
    return {"n": int(len(rs)), "mean": float(rs.mean()),
            "median": float(np.median(rs)), "win": float((rs > 0).mean()),
            "t": t, "worst": float(rs.min()), "best": float(rs.max())}


def build_weights(ts, o, c, params=None):
    p = dict(PARAMS)
    if params:
        p.update(params)
    f = daily_features(ts, o, c)
    pos, event_days, s = skew_state(f, p)
    w = weights_from_pos(ts, f, pos)
    runs = episodes(f, pos)
    info = dict(params=p, signal_days=int(len(event_days)),
                events=int(len(event_days)), episodes=len(runs),
                tqqq_exposure=float(np.mean(w[:, 1])),
                s10_mean=float(np.nanmean(s)), s10_min=float(np.nanmin(s)),
                s10_max=float(np.nanmax(s)),
                episode_stats=episode_stats(runs),
                event_forward=forward_event_stats(f, event_days, int(p["hold"])))
    return w, info

# evaluation

def metrics(pos, slip=1.0, start=DEV_START, end=DEV_END, w=None):
    if w is None:
        w = weights_from_pos(TS, F, pos)
    if start == DEV_START and end == DEV_END:
        r = bt.run(TS, O, C, w, start, band=0.02, slippage_bps=slip)
        s = bt.stats(r, BARS_PER_YEAR)
        ww = w
    else:
        i = bt.start_index(TS, start)
        j = int(TS.searchsorted(pd.Timestamp(end, tz="America/New_York"), side="right"))
        r = bt.simulate(TS[i:j], O[i:j], C[i:j], w[i:j], band=0.02,
                        slippage_bps=slip)
        s = bt.stats(r, BARS_PER_YEAR)
        ww = w[i:j]
    return {"cagr": s["cagr"], "max_drawdown": s["max_drawdown"],
            "sharpe": s["sharpe"], "sortino": s["sortino"],
            "volatility": s["volatility"], "fills": s["fills"],
            "turnover": s["turnover"], "ending_equity": s["ending_equity"],
            "tqqq_exposure": float(np.mean(ww[:, 1]))}


def daily_returns(pos, slip=1.0):
    r = bt.run(TS, O, C, weights_from_pos(TS, F, pos), DEV_START,
               band=0.02, slippage_bps=slip)
    eq = pd.Series(r["equity"], index=r["ts"])
    return eq.groupby(eq.index.date).last().pct_change().dropna()


def load_winner_returns(slug):
    path = ROOT / "research" / "new" / "curves" / f"{slug}.json"
    d = json.loads(path.read_text())
    dates = pd.to_datetime(d["dates"])
    keep = dates <= pd.Timestamp(DEV_END)
    vals = np.asarray(d["values"], dtype=float)[keep]
    return pd.Series(vals, index=dates[keep]).pct_change().dropna()


def correlations(pos):
    sr = daily_returns(pos)
    sr.index = pd.to_datetime(sr.index)
    out = {}
    for slug in WINNERS:
        wr = load_winner_returns(slug)
        j = sr.index.intersection(wr.index)
        out[slug] = float(np.corrcoef(sr.loc[j], wr.loc[j])[0, 1])
    tq = pd.Series(F["tq"], index=pd.to_datetime(F["sess_dates"]))
    tr = tq.pct_change().dropna()
    j = sr.index.intersection(tr.index)
    out["TQQQ"] = float(np.corrcoef(sr.loc[j], tr.loc[j])[0, 1])
    return out


def placebo(pos, event_days, params, n_draw=100, seed=11):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    real = metrics(pos)["cagr"]
    seg = pos[WARM:]
    shift_c = []
    for _ in range(n_draw):
        sh = int(rng.integers(20, len(seg) - 20))
        q = np.r_[np.zeros(WARM), np.roll(seg, sh)]
        shift_c.append(metrics(q)["cagr"])

    pool = np.arange(WARM, F["nd"] - 1)
    n_ev = len(event_days)
    rand_c, rand_e = [], []
    for _ in range(n_draw):
        pick = rng.choice(pool, n_ev, replace=False)
        mm = np.zeros(F["nd"], dtype=bool)
        mm[pick] = True
        q = np.zeros(F["nd"])
        until = -1
        for d in range(F["nd"]):
            if mm[d]:
                until = max(until, d + int(params["hold"]))
            if d < until:
                q[d] = 1.0
        m = metrics(q)
        rand_c.append(m["cagr"]); rand_e.append(m["tqqq_exposure"])

    def summ(v):
        a = np.asarray(v)
        return {"n_draws": int(len(a)), "mean_cagr": float(a.mean()),
                "std_cagr": float(a.std(ddof=1)),
                "p95_cagr": float(np.quantile(a, 0.95)),
                "max_cagr": float(a.max()),
                "p_value": float((a >= real).mean())}

    s = summ(shift_c)
    s["note"] = "circular shift of the daily target vector; preserves exposure, event count and clustering."
    r = summ(rand_c)
    r["mean_exposure"] = float(np.mean(rand_e))
    r["note"] = "same number of event days drawn uniformly; destroys timing and clustering."
    return {"real_cagr": real, "signal_days": n_ev, "shift": s,
            "random_entry": r}


def precut_check():
    cut = bt.start_index(TS, "2020-03-12")
    f = daily_features(TS[:cut], O[:cut], C[:cut])
    pos_cut, _, _ = skew_state(f, PARAMS)
    w_cut = weights_from_pos(TS[:cut], f, pos_cut)
    w_full = weights_from_pos(TS, F, F["pos"])
    pre = min(len(w_cut), cut)
    return {"cut": "2020-03-12 11:07 America/New_York",
            "bars_compared": int(pre),
            "max_abs_weight_diff": float(np.max(np.abs(
                w_cut[:pre, 1] - w_full[:pre, 1])))}

TS = O = C = F = None


def main():
    global TS, O, C, F
    TS, O, C = bt.panel(("QQQ", "TQQQ", "BIL"), DEV_START, DEV_END, "1min")
    F = daily_features(TS, O, C)
    pos, event_days, s10 = skew_state(F, PARAMS)
    F["pos"] = pos
    w = weights_from_pos(TS, F, pos)
    runs = episodes(F, pos)
    info = dict(params=PARAMS, signal_days=int(len(event_days)),
                events=int(len(event_days)), episodes=len(runs),
                tqqq_exposure=float(np.mean(w[:, 1])),
                s10_mean=float(np.nanmean(s10)), s10_min=float(np.nanmin(s10)),
                s10_max=float(np.nanmax(s10)),
                episode_stats=episode_stats(runs),
                event_forward=forward_event_stats(F, event_days, PARAMS["hold"]))

    out = {
        "agent": SLUG,
        "family": "intraday realized skewness",
        "idea": "Negative intraday realized skew marks a session whose "
                "downside tail dominates. The skew premium predicts a bounce "
                "over the next few sessions; positive skew is the fragile / "
                "lottery side.",
        "hypothesis": "Trailing 10-session realized skew below -0.10 is "
                      "followed by positive next-open TQQQ returns over three "
                      "sessions, enough to beat TQQQ's development CAGR with a "
                      "lower drawdown.",
        "universe": ["QQQ", "TQQQ", "BIL"],
        "window": {"dev": [DEV_START, DEV_END], "holdout": "not loaded"},
        "execution": {"engine": "research/bt.py", "marks": "1min",
                      "fills": "next open", "band": 0.02,
                      "headline_bps": 1.0, "also_bps": [5.0, 10.0],
                      "weight_cap": 1.0, "long_only": True,
                      "exposure_state": "TQQQ 1.0 after a negative-skew event, BIL otherwise"},
        "params": PARAMS, "info": info, "windows": {"dev": {}},
        "benchmarks": {}, "yearly": {}, "grid": [], "cuts": {},
        "placebo": {}, "corr_winners": {}, "corr_tqqq": None, "precut": {},
        "kill_criteria": [
            "dev 1 bp CAGR <= 36.72% or dev max drawdown >= 82.29%",
            "fewer than 5 of the 8 pre-registered grid cells clear the same bar",
            "10 bp CAGR <= 36.72%",
            "shift-placebo p > 0.05",
            "random-entry placebo p > 0.05",
            "ex-2020 CAGR <= 25%",
            "daily-return correlation to family-short-reversal > 0.85",
            "fewer than 100 fills or fewer than 30 independent events",
            "pre-cut max weight difference > 1e-12",
            "event-forward 3-session t <= 1.5 (skew premium absent at the event level)",
        ],
        "status": None,
    }

    for slip, lab in ((1.0, "1bp"), (5.0, "5bp"), (10.0, "10bp")):
        out["windows"]["dev"][lab] = metrics(pos, slip, w=w)
        if slip == 1.0:
            r1 = bt.run(TS, O, C, w, DEV_START, band=0.02, slippage_bps=1.0)

    out["benchmarks"]["tqqq"] = bt.benchmark(C[:, 1], TS, BARS_PER_YEAR)
    out["benchmarks"]["qqq"] = bt.benchmark(C[:, 0], TS, BARS_PER_YEAR)
    out["benchmarks"]["tqqq"]["note"] = (
        "1-minute marks; the task bar is 36.72% / 82.29% / 0.82 on daily closes.")
    out["yearly"] = {int(k): v for k, v in
                     bt.yearly(TS, r1["equity"], C[:, 1]).items()}

    cells = [
        ("1 s10 -0.10 h3 (primary)", dict(skew_thr=-0.10, hold=3)),
        ("2 s10 -0.05 h3", dict(skew_thr=-0.05, hold=3)),
        ("3 s10 -0.15 h3", dict(skew_thr=-0.15, hold=3)),
        ("4 s10 -0.20 h3", dict(skew_thr=-0.20, hold=3)),
        ("5 s10 -0.10 h2", dict(skew_thr=-0.10, hold=2)),
        ("6 s10 -0.10 h4", dict(skew_thr=-0.10, hold=4)),
        ("7 s10 -0.10 h5", dict(skew_thr=-0.10, hold=5)),
        ("8 s10 -0.10 h6", dict(skew_thr=-0.10, hold=6)),
    ]
    for name, pp in cells:
        p = dict(PARAMS); p.update(pp)
        q, _, _ = skew_state(F, p)
        out["grid"].append({"name": name, "params": pp, **metrics(q)})

    for name, a, b in (("2016-2019", "2016-01-04", "2019-12-31"),
                       ("2020-2021", "2020-01-02", "2021-12-31"),
                       ("2022-2023", "2022-01-03", "2023-12-29")):
        out["cuts"][name] = metrics(pos, 1.0, a, b, w)
    years = pd.Series(pd.to_datetime(list(F["dates"][F["first"]]))).dt.year.to_numpy()
    for y in (2020, 2022):
        q = pos.copy(); q[years == y] = 0.0
        out["cuts"][f"ex{y}"] = metrics(q)

    out["placebo"] = placebo(pos, event_days, PARAMS)
    out["corr_winners"] = correlations(pos)
    out["corr_tqqq"] = out["corr_winners"]["TQQQ"]
    out["precut"] = precut_check()

    dev = out["windows"]["dev"]["1bp"]
    n_grid = sum(1 for g in out["grid"]
                 if g["cagr"] > 0.3672 and g["max_drawdown"] < 0.8229)
    primary_ok = dev["cagr"] > 0.3672 and dev["max_drawdown"] < 0.8229
    if primary_ok and n_grid >= 5 and out["placebo"]["shift"]["p_value"] <= 0.05:
        out["status"] = ("dev_pass" if out["windows"]["dev"]["10bp"]["cagr"] > 0.3672
                         else "dev_pass_marginal")
    elif primary_ok:
        out["status"] = "dev_pass_marginal"
    else:
        out["status"] = "dev_fail"
    out["grid_cells_above_bar"] = int(n_grid)

    (OUT / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2, default=float))
    print(json.dumps({
        "status": out["status"],
        "primary": {k: out["windows"]["dev"][k] for k in ("1bp", "5bp", "10bp")},
        "grid_cells_above_bar": n_grid,
        "corr_tqqq": out["corr_tqqq"],
        "corr_range": [min(out["corr_winners"][s] for s in WINNERS),
                       max(out["corr_winners"][s] for s in WINNERS)],
        "placebo": out["placebo"], "precut": out["precut"],
        "info": {k: v for k, v in info.items() if k != "episode_stats"},
    }, indent=2, default=float))
    print("wrote", OUT / "result.json")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
